counterfactual_missing_items: monoclonal protein or abnormal free-light-chain ratio
response.rationale: R5 is favored because noncaseating granulomatous hepatitis directly anchors a granulomatous disease, and the combination of hypercalcemia with low PTH (9 ng/L), normal phosphorus, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, and hepatosplenic plus osteolytic distribution fits sarcoidosis. R2 can explain osteolytic skull and visceral nodules but lacks tissue confirmation of Langerhans cells and does not explain the hypercalcemia/low-PTH pattern. R3 is contradicted by absent monoclonal protein and normal free-light-chain ratio; R4 by low PTH with normal phosphorus; R1 by absence of vitamin D exposure.

rejected.why: Only raw support is hypercalcemia; there is no history of vitamin D supplementation and it cannot explain granulomatous hepatitis, osteolytic lesions, or suppressed PTH.
Despite hypercalcemia, anemia, renal failure, and osteolytic lesions, it is directly contradicted by no monoclonal peak and normal serum free light-chain ratio, with unremarkable bone marrow biopsy.
The low PTH of 9 ng/L and normal phosphorus directly contradict hyperparathyroidism and no adenoma or PTH-dependent mechanism is supported.
